gloss: to come; to visit (humble); to appear on the scene

definitions.explanation: A humble expression meaning to go or come to someone of higher status. Historically used by samurai and retainers when presenting themselves before a lord.

definitions.gloss: to appear on the scene; to show up
definitions.explanation: Used in a dramatic or playful way to announce one's arrival, often with a heroic or theatrical flair. Common in anime, manga, and entertainment.

examples.japanese: ただいま{参上|さんじょう}いたしました。
お{招|まね}きいただき、{喜|よろこ}んで{参上|さんじょう}いたします。
examples.english: Thank you for the invitation — I will gladly come.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}、{改|あらた}めて{参上|さんじょう}いたしますので、よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I will come again tomorrow, so please bear with me.

examples.japanese: {正義|せいぎ}の{味方|みかた}、ここに{参上|さんじょう}！
examples.english: The hero of justice has arrived!

examples.japanese: {助|たす}けを{求|もと}める{声|こえ}を{聞|き}いて{参上|さんじょう}した。
examples.english: He appeared on the scene after hearing a cry for help.

examples.japanese: お{困|こま}りのようですね。{私|わたし}が{参上|さんじょう}しましょう！
examples.english: You seem to be in trouble. Allow me to come to the rescue!

notes:
Originally a humble verb used when presenting oneself before someone of higher rank, {参上|さんじょう}する retains this formal, deferential meaning in business and ceremonial contexts. In modern popular culture, however, it has taken on a dramatic, heroic connotation — characters in anime and period dramas announce their arrival with {参上|さんじょう}! as a declaration of presence.

USAGE:
- In formal/humble use, typically paired with いたす: {参上|さんじょう}いたします
- In dramatic/playful use, often stands alone as an exclamation: {参上|さんじょう}！

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {参上|さんじょう}いたします: I will come (humble)
- ただいま{参上|さんじょう}: I have just arrived
- ここに{参上|さんじょう}: arrived here (dramatic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {伺|うかが}う: to visit (humble) — the standard humble verb for visiting; {参上|さんじょう}する is more literary and dramatic
- {参|まい}る: to go; to come (humble) — general humble movement verb without the theatrical associations
